Spot premium quotations for imported cathode fell over the past two weeks as the negative arbitrage between the SHFE and the LME widened. Traders reported that the latest spot premium quotations for imported cathode and SXEW cathode had both been quoted between US$30/t and US$50/t, with major traders offering cathode at around US$40-50/t. Very few deals were closed due to the significant import loss. We recently heard reports that there is some cathode stock building up in Shanghai bonded warehouses that is being readied for re-export. Similarly, we also noticed that cathode inventories © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **March 2012** www.crugroup.com increased in LME Asian warehouses. We will continue to monitor cathode movements involving the LME Asian warehouses to check whether it persists. According to Chinese customs data, China imported 375,831t and exported 700t of cathode in February. Cathode exports did not increase significantly and we expect that they may go up in March in part due to smelters export cathode through the concentrate tolling business. We believe that the cathode import data in March will be critical for the short term market sentiment. Market insiders’ expect cathode imports to decline. However, if imports continue to increase, or remain at very high levels, the short term market outlook may turn gloomier as market participants would expect sustained high levels of imports of cathode to put additional pressure on supply in a market where the demand prospect are already lacklustre. We were told by market insiders that the cathode inventories in bonded warehouses currently were around 550,000t, thus maintaining the upward trend. We attribute this to traders attempting to avoid incurring losses by not selling imported metal on the spot market where prices are currently low. # Growth rates in copper semis output may decline soon According to the vice president of Hailiang Group, a leading copper tube producer in China, who was presenting at a Copper Conference in Shanghai last week, there are challenges ahead for copper semis producers. He said that high and volatile copper prices, semis overcapacity, a slow-down in end-use and a tight credit market are the main problems. Facility utilisation at most semis producers’

declined in recent years as semis capacity has continued to expand.  We believe that the different types of copper semis have had different peak expansion periods, each lasting 2-3 years.  Copper tube started in 2001, copper plate, sheet and strip (PSS) from 2006, copper wirerod from 2009 and copper foil started in 2010. The tube industry has reached maturity and there are almost no large projects expected in the future. Wirerod and PSS producers are struggling with overcapacity problems.  Foil products are still not competitive in the international high-end products market.  Copper semis capacity expansions will therefore be constrained by overcapacity, reduced profit and increasing production costs in the future. However, competitive pressures to move up the value chain should see investment in high value added products (e.g. plate, sheet, strip, and foil (PSSF)). 

Going forward, we were told by some small and mid-range semis producers that they will have to halt production in the short term due to a lack of new orders this year.  Slowing production is also reflected in CNIA data.  The average monthly growth of China’s semis production slowed down to less than 5% in 2011 compared to about 18% in 2010.  In addition, semis products inventories have begun to build up. Looking further ahead, China’s copper demand may enter into a high base and low growth period, as GDP growth slows down.  At the same time, RMB appreciation, macro controls and the transformation of the economy are expected to affect copper semis industry.  Moreover, semis products demand also faces continual substitution threats.

# The outlook for copper consumption in home 

# appliances in 2012 

During a domestic copper conference in Shanghai this Friday, China's home appliance association released a report giving some indication of the copper consumption prospects in the home appliance industry in 2012.  China's home appliance output growth slowed down after high growth rates in 2011. The growth rate in the export value of home appliances declined to 17.6%.  While the stimulus policy continues to support the home appliance industry, home appliance sales in the urban areas fell due to severe macro controls on the property market.  Looking ahead, the negative factors affecting the white goods industry include the global economic turmoil; RMB appreciation; volatile commodity prices and the withdrawal of the stimulus package.  At the same time, the opportunities include the effects on demand of continuing urbanisation; potential social housing construction in 2H 2012; lower inflation and opportunities for industry upgrading.  China's home appliance association forecasts that the home appliance sales value growth may decelerate to 10 -15% in 2012 and growth in the export value may be reduced to 10%.  Moreover, high and volatile copper prices may accelerate copper minimization design

and substitution efforts. Overall, the utilisation rates of home appliances are expected to decrease in 2012. However, the operations of home appliance enterprises may improve as product inventories decline gradually in 2H 2012. # Copper prices stay range bound SHFE 3-month price

The LME 3-month copper price has continued to trade in the narrow $8,200-8,600/t range that it has been in since rising back above $8,000/t in mid-January, with fluctuations driven by economic data releases. The SHFE 3-month copper price fluctuated between RMB59,760-60,780/t in the past two weeks. Given the poor demand for cathode, the market in China remains in contango, with the Shanghai physical price below the SHFE cash-month price and the SHFE cash-month price below the 3-month price. SHFE cathode inventories have fallen slightly from the almost 10-year peak reached 2 weeks ago. Last week inventory fell by 3,644t, and this week by another 4,818t to 218,814t. The SHFE stocks in bonded © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 4 **March 2012** www.crugroup.com warehouses continued to climb, rising by 2,972t over the past two weeks, while the tax-paid tonnage fell by 11,434t. Given that bonded stock inflows come from imports, this difference supports the view that imports have remained high over the past two weeks. Low physical demand and the contango in forward prices mean that prices should be under downward pressure. However, the 100-day moving average (as shown in the price chart on the previous page) has flattened out, which indicates technical support for copper prices. Until there is a strong signal that prompts a change in sentiment higher or lower, we expect the SHFE 3-month copper price will remain stuck in the range between RMB59,000/t to RMB61,000/t during the following two weeks. #### **Questions or comments may be addressed to:** **Grace Qu (Beijing):** +86 10 6510 2206, ext. 321 grace.qu@crugroup.com **Miljan Sladoje (London):** +44 207 903 2062 miljan.sladoje@crugroup.com This issue was completed on 30th March, 2012.
